S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is characterized by at least one lifetime manic episode, typically lasting at least one week and causing marked impairment in social or occupational functioning, often requiring hospitalization. Manic episodes involve a distinct period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased energy or activity, frequently accompanied by inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts, distractibility, and risky or goal-directed behaviors. Depressive episodes are common but not required for the diagnosis, and the course is often recurrent with variable periods of remission between episodes. It is distinguished from Bipolar II Disorder by the presence of full mania rather than hypomania, and from primary psychotic disorders by the episodic nature of mood symptoms and their temporal relationship to any psychotic features.

patient.personality: Miguel is a laid-back but seasoned kitchen supervisor who combines curiosity for new recipes with a pragmatic, steady approach to keeping his team and restaurant running smoothly.
patient.stressor: Miguel’s difficulties started after his divorce was finalized and his adult children moved farther away for work, leaving him living alone for the first time in decades while also being promoted to oversee a second kitchen location. On paper the promotion was a recognition of his experience, but the combination of longer hours, commuting between sites, and coming home to an empty apartment disrupted the familiar routines that had anchored him. He coped by throwing himself into work—experimenting with new menu ideas, volunteering for extra shifts, and staying late to mentor younger cooks—then filling his off-hours with car restoration, community cooking workshops, and late-night soccer games on TV, rarely allowing himself downtime. Over seven months, his days blurred into one another, with colleagues noting he seemed to function on almost no rest and was increasingly hard to redirect when he fixated on new ideas, until a concerned manager and a cousin noticed how worn but “wired” he looked and persuaded him to see his primary care doctor, who referred him to psychiatry.
patient.chief_complaint: I’m only sleeping a few hours a night but I still feel like I can just keep going, and my family is worried it’s not normal.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days lately I swing between feeling on top of the world, joking and buzzing around both kitchens, to snapping at my line cooks over little things like how they chop an onion, and it can flip like a light switch over something small like a late delivery or a dirty pan.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: It’s like I’ve got a motor in me that won’t shut off—I’ll run both kitchens all day, then go home and tear apart the carburetor on my old Chevy or plan a whole new menu until two or three in the morning without ever actually sitting still.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I catch myself thinking, ‘I’m the only one in this whole company who really knows how to run a kitchen,’ like I could turn these two restaurants into a whole chain if people would just keep up with my ideas, which is way more full of myself than I usually am.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: For months now I’ll fall asleep around two or three, wake up at five or six without an alarm, and instead of feeling tired I pop right up and start making elaborate breakfast plans for the staff, like my body doesn’t care that I barely slept.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: At work or at home I’ll start on one thing—like writing the order list—and then a pot clanging, a game on the TV, or a new recipe popping into my head pulls me off in another direction, so I leave half-finished lists, half-fixed car parts, and ten browser tabs open without really meaning to.
